answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in a vault and pledges a saffron crate to the depot. The depot weighs it and logs its seal publicly. Each gale, auditors re-weigh crates; a light, reused, or missing crate burns its bond. First crate costs 38, the k-th 38+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,035,000 and lock 70,000, against a 40,000 pool. Rented crates fail: one shared seal burns both. An honest agent pays 38 once and reclaims it after a clean audit.
